summary: Breaks down a full `ansible-playbook` command line, explaining the inventory, remote user, SSH password prompt, forks, timeout, tags, module path, become, and become-password flags.
questions: What do the -k and -K flags mean for ansible-playbook?
How do I run only tasks with a certain tag from the command line?
How can I set the number of parallel forks and a connection timeout when running a playbook?
How do I point ansible-playbook at a custom inventory file and a local modules directory?
How do I run a playbook with sudo and get prompted for the sudo password?

answer_card.title: Common ansible-playbook flags
answer_card.answer_md:
```bash
ansible-playbook -i /path/to/my_inventory_file -u my_connection_user -k -f 3 -T 30 -t my_tag -M /path/to/my_modules -b -K my_playbook.yml
```
- `-i` inventory file
- `-u` SSH user to connect as
- `-k` prompt for the SSH password
- `-f` number of forks (here 3)
- `-T` connection timeout in seconds
- `-t` run only tasks with this tag
- `-M` path to local modules
- `-b` use become (privilege escalation)
- `-K` prompt for the become password
